news.headline: Nasdaq 100 Enters Official Correction, Down 10% From October Peak on AI Rout
news.body: The Nasdaq 100 fell as much as 4.5% on October 30, crossing the 10% decline threshold from its October 6 all-time high and entering its third technical correction of 2026. The broader Nasdaq Composite recorded its worst day since June, closing down nearly 3% at 25,437, capping the index's worst month since March 2025. The sell-off wiped roughly $2 trillion from Nasdaq-100 market value across the week, driven by earnings misses at Intel, Amazon, Alphabet, ServiceNow, and Reddit. Traders rotated into Treasuries and defensive sectors, while the VIX surged roughly 23% to near 21.

news.headline: Reddit Plunges ~29% on Soft Q4 Revenue Outlook, Worst Day Since 2024 IPO
news.body: Reddit shares tumbled approximately 29% on October 30, their steepest decline since the company's 2024 IPO, after the social media platform issued a Q4 revenue forecast below Wall Street estimates and announced it would restrict access to its message boards to registered account holders. The stock closed near $91.73 after the company reported Q3 results that beat on earnings and revenue but failed to offset concerns about decelerating user-monetization growth. Roblox fell an additional 17–20% the same session after daily active users declined 9% year-over-year, illustrating how ad-dependent platforms are being punished for growth deceleration. The combined sell-off added material pressure to the Nasdaq Composite on the final trading day of October.

news.headline: Exxon, Chevron Beat Q3 Estimates as Refining Profits Surge on Higher Diesel Prices
news.body: ExxonMobil and Chevron both topped Q3 2026 consensus estimates on October 30, lifted by soaring refining margins as diesel prices reached roughly $6.32 per gallon—up 71% year-over-year—amid supply disruptions tied to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. ExxonMobil reported adjusted EPS of $4.23 versus the $4.12 estimate on $15.4 billion in GAAP earnings and $25.7 billion in operating cash flow, while Chevron posted adjusted EPS of $5.28 on net earnings of $9.9 billion, up nearly 200% year-over-year. Exxon also cut net debt by nearly $11 billion year-to-date and returned $9.4 billion to shareholders in the quarter; Chevron raised its quarterly dividend by 5.2%. Both stocks rose roughly 1–2% during a session when the broader market sold off sharply.

news.headline: Amazon Falls ~7% as Q3 Capex Surges to $77.3B, Misses EPS and Revenue
news.body: Amazon (AMZN) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.89 vs. $1.96 expected and revenue of $201.94B vs. $202.10B consensus, while capital expenditures ballooned to $77.3B—far above the $58.7B expected—pushing trailing 12-month free cash flow to a record negative $42.4B. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 capex target of ~$220B, driven by aggressive AI and AWS buildout; AWS itself grew 39% to $45.98B, the fastest pace in nearly five years. Shares fell roughly 7% premarket Friday before settling down ~2–3%, adding fuel to the broader AI spending concern narrative that hit Alphabet and Intel earlier in the week.

news.headline: Intel Crashes ~29%, Worst Day Since 1974, Wiping $150B in Market Value
news.body: Intel shares plunged roughly 29% on October 30—their worst single-session loss since 1974—after the chipmaker forecast Q4 revenue of $15–$16 billion, more than $1 billion below Wall Street's $17 billion estimate, and guided for no positive free cash flow this year. The sell-off erased approximately $150 billion in market cap and delivered a roughly $12 billion blow to the U.S. government, which holds a 10% stake. Semiconductor peers SanDisk and Qualcomm dropped 13% and 11%, respectively, deepening the broader chip-sector rout. The disaster overshadowed Intel's data-center revenue growth of nearly 80% year-over-year, underscoring that PC weakness and fab-capacity constraints are dominating investor sentiment.

news.headline: China Stocks Log Worst Monthly Loss Since 2016 as AI Selloff Deepens
news.body: China's blue-chip CSI 300 fell 1.4% on October 30, closing near a one-year low and capping its steepest monthly decline since early 2016, while Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index plunged 5.5%. The selloff was driven by a global rotation out of AI-linked equities after disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel reignited fears about the returns on heavy artificial-intelligence capital expenditure. The Shanghai Composite shed 1.44% to 3,599 and the Shenzhen Component lost 2.73%, with SAIC Motor, Avic Aviation Engine, and Yonyou Software among the session's biggest losers. The 12th consecutive weekly loss for mainland benchmarks underscores mounting concern that China's AI-driven equity rally has run well ahead of earnings fundamentals.

news.headline: Binance Suffers Record $6.3B Crypto Heist Linked to North Korea, Halts Withdrawals
news.body: Attackers drained approximately $6.36 billion from Binance wallets across ten blockchains in roughly 20 minutes on the night of October 29–30, the largest crypto theft on record — four times the size of the 2025 Bybit hack. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor; about $3 billion in assets have been frozen. Binance, headquartered in the region and the world's largest exchange by volume, suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover all user losses, setting aside ~$6 billion. The hack sent Bitcoin below $77,000 and triggered broad risk-off sentiment across crypto-exposed Asian listed names and fintech stocks.

news.headline: China Optical Module Trio Drops 8–20% Despite Strong Q3 Earnings as AI Capex Doubts Mount
news.body: Shares of Zhongji Innolight, Eoptolink Technology, and TFC Optical fell 8.5%, 11.1%, and 19.8% respectively on October 30 in Shenzhen — extending a two-day rout despite all three reporting strong Q3 results driven by AI data-centre demand. Eoptolink dropped as much as 15% intraday; the stocks are now 56–60% below their June/July 2026 highs. Citi cut its 2026–2027 earnings forecasts for the sector by 19%, citing slower revenue recognition and a more cautious ramp-up for optical engines. Investor concern centres on whether heavy US hyperscaler AI capex will sustain offshore demand, compounded by ongoing risk of US import restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers.

news.headline: PAG Buys 51% of Evergrande Property Services for $510M in Largest Liquidation Asset Sale
news.body: Hong Kong private equity firm PAG agreed to acquire a 51% controlling stake in Evergrande Property Services (6666.HK) from China Evergrande's liquidators for HK$4.03 billion (~$514 million), the largest single asset sale in Evergrande's liquidation to date. The per-share price of HK$0.8359 represented a 29.5% discount to the pre-halt close, and shares resumed October 30 to fall 17.72% to HK$0.98. PAG will launch a mandatory general offer at the same price for remaining shares, valuing the whole company at ~HK$9 billion. The deal signals institutional appetite for China's property-services sector and marks tangible recovery progress for offshore creditors who had recouped less than 1% of the $46 billion owed.

news.headline: BOJ Holds at 1.25% with Hawkish Lean, Accelerates ETF Disposal Pace More Than 2x
news.body: The Bank of Japan kept its overnight policy rate at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote on October 30, with dissenter Hajime Takata pushing for a 25 bp hike to 1.50%, signalling underlying CPI is now 'generally consistent' with the 2% target — a language upgrade from July. The BOJ also voted unanimously to more than double its ETF disposal pace to ~¥860 billion per year from January 2027, cutting the unwind timeline from 112 to 43 years. The hawkish hold reinforced December hike expectations, though market odds slipped to ~68% from ~77%. The Nikkei 225 fell 2.12% on the day as chip-sector selling compounded the rate uncertainty.

news.headline: Brent Settles at 6-Month High as Tanker Struck by Mines in Strait of Hormuz
news.body: Brent crude futures settled up 2.4% at $117.64/bbl on Oct 30—its highest close since end-April—and posted a 13.6% monthly gain (WTI +15.2%) as its fourth consecutive monthly advance. The British military confirmed a commercial tanker was struck by explosive devices attached from a small boat while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, temporarily disabling the vessel; Iran's Revolutionary Guard separately claimed three additional tankers struck naval mines on Oct 30. With IMF PortWatch recording only 2 daily transits versus a pre-crisis baseline of 85, freight costs have surged to ~$21/bbl vs $6.50 in September. Markets are pricing elevated risk of post-midterm US escalation against Iran, keeping a significant war premium embedded in crude.

news.headline: Gold Crashes to One-Year Low Below $3,900 as Fed Hike Bets, Tech Rout Trigger Liquidations
news.body: Spot gold fell as much as 3.2% to $3,891.67/oz on Oct 30—its weakest level since October 2025—while silver plunged 5.7% to ~$49.00, breaching $50 for the first time since November 2025. The selloff was driven by stronger-than-expected US Q3 GDP and PCE inflation data hardening December Fed rate hike bets to ~85%, compounded by forced liquidations as AI/tech stocks fell sharply. Gold is now down roughly 30% from its January 2026 record near $5,595 and on track for its worst October since 2008; major gold miners including Kinross shed 7.7% on the day, with the five largest North American producers losing ~$140bn from their 52-week highs.

news.headline: European TTF Gas Surges 4.9% to €102.78/MWh, Hitting 4-Year High on Record-Low Storage
news.body: Dutch TTF December futures rose 4.9% to €102.78/MWh on Oct 30—up ~36% in October and ~256% year-to-date—the highest since December 2022 as EU gas storage sits at just 75% of capacity, the lowest for this time of year since records began in 2011. Qatari LNG flows through the blocked Strait of Hormuz have fallen to a fraction of pre-war levels, and Europe's LNG imports ran 30% below year-earlier levels in early October. Analysts warn prices could spike to €130/MWh in early 2027 if severe cold weather coincides with continued supply disruption, with a potential 0.5% GDP drag on Europe.

news.headline: Silver Miners Plunge 6-8% as Spot Silver Drops 5.7% Below $50 on Fed Rate Fears
news.body: Spot silver fell 5.7% to ~$49.00/oz on Oct 30, breaking below the psychologically important $50 level for the first time since November 2025 and extending its October loss to ~14% since Oct 19. The Federal Reserve held its target rate at 3.75–4.00% this week but two policymakers voted for an immediate hike, and futures now price ~85% probability of a December increase. Silver miners tracked losses sharply: Hecla Mining -5.8%, Coeur Mining -6%, Endeavour Silver -6.2%, Silvercorp Metals -5.7%; iShares Silver Trust dropped 5.2%.

news.headline: Copper Posts First Monthly Loss Since June as AI Spending Doubts Weigh; LME Down 1.5%
news.body: LME three-month copper fell 1.5% to $14,140/ton on Oct 30, its lowest in a week, locking in a ~1.3% October decline—the metal's first monthly loss since June—as disappointing tech earnings sparked fresh doubts about AI infrastructure returns and the copper demand tied to it. BNP Paribas noted post-LME Week that 'few participants believed AI was a significant driver of copper demand,' compounding the hit from higher oil prices and macro risk-off sentiment. Physical tightness persists: the Yangshan premium for Chinese imports held near a 13-year high of $205/ton and LME cash backwardation remained elevated, limiting the downside.
